script: Spread and total were not saved, so the HOU@TEN script is inferred only from form. Houston cannot run it — David Montgomery is 27 carries for 67 yards (2.5 YPC) and Woody Marks 19 for 45 (2.4 YPC) over weeks 2-4 — so C.J. Stroud has to throw, and Tennessee blitzes only 22%, the look where his EPA/dropback is -0.03. Tennessee wants Tony Pollard (47 carries, 186 yards) until Houston's 3.44 YPC run defense and 8 runs of 10+ stall him and Cam Ward has to throw.
who_goes_off: Dalton Schultz is the Houston move-the-chains target: 19 targets, 179 receiving yards and only 135 air yards over weeks 2-4, a 59.7-yard pace versus a 34.0 line. Carnell Tate is the Tennessee shot: 26 targets, 230 yards and 312 air yards (76.7 per game) against a 46.5 line, not Nico Collins, who has just 8 targets and 118 yards in that same three-game window.
weak_spot: Houston's leak is the middle, not the outside corners: 9.95 YPA on 38 middle attempts versus 5.40 YPA on 43 left attempts and 8.35 on 60 right, with 17 gains of 20+ yards on 156 attempts. Tennessee is flatter by location — middle 8.21 on 24 attempts, left 8.10 on 40, right 7.52 on 48 — and softer on the ground at 3.88 YPC with 11 runs of 10+ and only 13 passes of 20+ on 120 attempts.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for HOU@TEN, so there is no absence to reprice; Dalton Schultz's 19 targets and Carnell Tate's 26 targets over weeks 2-4 are treated as their current roles.
qb_vs_blitz: C.J. Stroud is +0.47 EPA/dropback versus blitz (n=34) and -0.03 with no blitz, but Tennessee blitzes only 22%, so he lives in the negative split and on Dalton Schultz's 135-air-yard, 179-yard diet. Cam Ward is +0.14 versus blitz (n=30) and -0.17 without it, and Houston blitzes only 21%, so Ward is mostly in his bad split — the outlet is Carnell Tate's 312 air yards into that 9.95 middle YPA.

picks.why: Schultz has 179 yards on 19 targets over weeks 2-4 (59.7 per game, 9.4 yards per target) against a 34.0 line, and his 135 air yards fit Stroud's no-blitz script (Tennessee 22% blitz, Stroud -0.03 EPA without pressure) into Tennessee's highest location mark, 8.21 YPA in the middle.

Tate has 230 yards on 26 targets and 312 air yards over weeks 2-4 (76.7 per game, 8.8 yards per target) against a 46.5 line, and Houston allows 9.95 YPA in the middle plus 17 passes of 20+ yards while holding rushers to 3.44 YPC, which pushes Cam Ward off Pollard's 47-carry diet and onto Tate.
